## Introduction

This assignment reinforces your practical skills in R programming
fundamentals, data structures, data cleaning, and Exploratory Data
Analysis (EDA) using the dplyr and ggplot2 packages. We will be working
with the provided episode data in BreakingBadData.csv.

## Dataset Overview

The dataset contains the following columns: - `Season`: The season
number of the episode. - `Title`: The title of the episode. - `Airdate`:
The air date of the episode. - `Rating`: The IMDb rating of the
episode. - `Vote_count`: The number of votes the episode received. -
`Description`: A brief description of the episode.

Let's load the dataset and start working!

#####Tasks##### #Task 1: Load all necessery libraries Ensure the needed
libraries are loaded and ready for use. If a library is not installed,
include code to install it.

```{r}
#Installing the needed packages
#install.packages("ggplot2")
#install.packages(("dplyr"))
```

#Task 2: Load the Dataset 1. Loads the CSV file 2. Prints the first few rows using head()

```{r}
#Loading the data and printing the first 5 rows
dataset <- read.csv("BreakingBadData.csv")
head(dataset)
```

### Task 3: Data Cleaning

The task is to ensure the `Airdate` column is treated as a `Date` type
and remove rows with missing values.

```{r}
#Setting the correct date format
dataset$Airdate <- as.Date(dataset$Airdate)
#Deleting all rows with empty values while creating a new, "clean" data set
bb_data_clean <- na.omit(dataset)
str(bb_data_clean)

```

#Task 4: Basic Conditionals

1.  Boolean Variable: Calculate the average IMDb rating of all episodes
    in bb_data_clean. Create a boolean variable is_high_rated that gets
    TRUE if the average is greater than 9.0, and FALSE otherwise.

```{r}
#Calculating the mean rating
avgRating = mean(bb_data_clean$Rating)
print(avgRating) #checking that there are no mistakes
is_high_rated <- avgRating > 9.0 #The condition - true if mean is greater than 9' false otherwise
```

2.  Conditional Statement: Write an if-else statement that prints one of
    two messages based on the value of is_high_rated: "The entire series
    is considered very highly rated!" or "The average rating does not
    pass the 9.0 threshold."

```{r}
if(is_high_rated){
  print("The entire series is considered very highly rated!")
}else{
  print("The average rating does not pass the 9.0 threshold.")
}

```

#Task 5: Loops for Episode Identification

1.For Loop: Write a for loop that iterates over the episodes in
bb_data_clean. If an episode's rating is equal to 10.0, print its Title
and its Vote_count.

```{r}
#Iterate through our clean data, print title and vote count for each value with 10.0 rating
for(i in 1:nrow(bb_data_clean)){
  if(bb_data_clean$Rating[i] == 10.0){
    print(paste(bb_data_clean$Title[i],bb_data_clean$Vote_count[i]))
  }
}
```

2.  While Loop: Write a while loop that counts how many episodes have a
    rating below 8.5. Print the final count.

```{r}
#Initialize counter for episodes with values lower than 8.5
count_low_rated = 0
#Initialize index to 1
i <- 1
#Run while there are still values in out data
while(i<nrow(bb_data_clean)){
  if(bb_data_clean$Rating[i] < 8.5){
    count_low_rated <- count_low_rated + 1 #Update the counter
  }
  i <- i + 1# Update the index
}
print(paste("We have " , count_low_rated, "values under 8.5 rating"))

```

#Task 6: Data Manipulation (dplyr Pipeline) Use the Pipe Operator (%\>%)
and a sequence of dplyr functions on bb_data_clean to create a summary
Data Frame. Assign the final result to the variable season_summary_df.

The pipeline must perform these steps sequentially: 1. group_by(): Group
the data by Season. 2. summarize(): Calculate the average rating
(avg_rating) and the total vote count (total_votes) for each season. 3.
mutate(): Add a new column is_top_rated_season that gets TRUE if the
avg_rating is greater than 9.2, and FALSE otherwise. 4. select(): Select
only the columns: Season, avg_rating, and is_top_rated_season.

```{r}
library(dplyr)#Calling the library
#Start streaming the data into season_summary_df

season_summary_df <- bb_data_clean%>%
  group_by(Season) %>%
  summarize(
    avgRating = mean(Rating),
    totalVotes = sum(Vote_count)
  ) %>%
  
  #Add the new boolean coloumn, then print it
  mutate(is_top_rated_season = avgRating > 9.2) %>% 
  select(Season, avgRating,is_top_rated_season)

print(season_summary_df)
  
```

#Task 7: Visualization (ggplot2) Create two plots using the ggplot2
library based on the cleaned data (bb_data_clean): 1. Bar Plot: Create a
Bar Plot showing the number of episodes in each season (Season).

```{r}
library(ggplot2)#Calling the library, then creating the bar plot - x = seasons, y = number of episodes
ggplot(bb_data_clean, aes(x = factor(Season))) + 
  geom_bar(fill ="darkseagreen1", color = "darkgreen") + 
  labs(title = "Number of Episodes per Season", x = "Season", y = "Episode count")

```

2.  Box Plot: Create a Box Plot to compare the distribution of the
    ratings (Rating) across the different seasons (Season).

```{r}
#Creating the box plot. x = season, y = rating
ggplot(bb_data_clean, aes(x=factor(Season), y = Rating)) + 
  geom_boxplot(fill = "darkgreen") + 
  labs(title = "Boxplot by Seasons", x = "Season", y = "Rating")

```
